excerpt: Selecting a commercial cleaning contractor solely on the lowest monthly lump sum almost guarantees chronic missed tasks and 90-day crew turnover. Use this 100-point weighted evaluation rubric to score janitorial scope of work (SOW) proposals across labor math, equipment specs, insurance verification, and SLA accountability.
quickAnswer: A defensible weighted evaluation rubric for a janitorial scope of work (SOW) checklist assigns 30% to Labor Hour & ISSA Production Realism (3,500 sq ft/hr at $35–$65/hr), 25% to Zone-by-Zone Scope & Frequency Alignment (using 4.33 weeks/month), 20% to Pricing Transparency ($0.07–$0.15/sq ft mid-market benchmarks), 15% to Equipment & Chemical Specs (4-level HEPA vacuums, EPA disinfectants), and 10% to W-2 Insurance & QA Governance. Any bidder scoring below 75/100 or failing a mandatory COI check should be disqualified.

blocks.text: Why Unweighted Janitorial Bid Comparisons Fail Procurement Committees

When three janitorial contractors respond to your Request for Proposal (RFP) for a 12,000 sq ft corporate office at 5x/week service (21.65 visits/month), their bottom-line quotes rarely cluster together. Vendor A bids $1,950/month, Vendor B bids $2,850/month, and Vendor C bids $3,400/month. Without a weighted evaluation rubric tied directly to your janitorial scope of work (SOW) checklist, corporate finance teams reflexively push to award the contract to Vendor A.

A structured 100-point scoring matrix exposes why Vendor A is a liability rather than a bargain. By scoring proposals across five quantitative dimensions—hourly labor math, task-frequency fidelity, transparent add-on pricing, commercial equipment capability, and risk compliance—you prove mathematically when a low bid violates the 3,500 sq ft/hour ISSA cleaning ceiling or relies on uninsured 1099 sub-crews.

blocks.title: Enforce Two Pass/Fail Gatekeeper Criteria Before Scoring
blocks.text: Before entering any vendor into the 100-point rubric, verify two non-negotiable prerequisites: (1) direct W-2 employee status backed by a current Workers' Compensation policy and a $1M/$2M General Liability Certificate of Insurance (COI) naming your entity as Additional Insured, and (2) explicit acceptance of 4.33-week monthly calendar amortization (21.65 visits/mo for 5x/wk). If either is missing, reject the bid immediately.
The 100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric for Janitorial SOW Proposals

Distribute this scoring table to every stakeholder on your facility evaluation committee. Each category carries a defined point weight and concrete pass, caution, and fail thresholds anchored to 2026 US commercial janitorial benchmarks.

blocks.text: Scoring Category 1 & 3: Auditing Labor Math and Square-Foot Rate Brackets

Together, Labor Realism (30 points) and Unit Pricing Transparency (20 points) account for half of the total evaluation score. To grade a vendor objectively, test their proposal against two cross-checks: the square-foot size bracket and the implied hourly wage calculation.

First, compare the bidder's per-visit square-foot price against your building's size bracket and frequency multiplier. For an office under 2,500 sq ft, legitimate rates run $0.12 to $0.20/sq ft (subject to a $90–$135 minimum visit charge). For 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft, expect $0.09 to $0.15/sq ft; for 10,000 to 24,999 sq ft, $0.07 to $0.12/sq ft; and for 25,000+ sq ft, $0.05 to $0.10/sq ft. Adjust those baselines by your frequency multiplier—1.08x for 1x/week (4.33 visits/mo), 1.00x for 2x/week (8.66 visits/mo), 0.95x for 3x/week (13.0 visits/mo), and 0.90x for 5x/week (21.65 visits/mo)—plus your flooring multiplier (1.00x carpet, 1.04x VCT/LVT, 1.05x mixed, 1.08x hardwood, 1.12x ceramic tile/grout, or 0.95x polished concrete).

blocks.text: Scoring Category 4: Verifying Commercial Hardware and Vacuum Specs (15 Points)

A vendor can only hit the ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hour production benchmark without kicking dust back into your HVAC return air if their crews deploy true commercial-grade equipment. Award the full 15 equipment points only when the bidder's SOW submittal explicitly commits to high-capacity, ergonomic hardware suited for modern commercial offices:

items: HEPA Backpack Vacuum Fleet: Require commercial backpack units rather than slow residential upright sweepers—specifically benchmarking against the ProTeam Super Coach Pro 6 Commercial Backpack Vacuum (6-quart capacity, 4-level HEPA filtration, lightweight 11.5 lb ergonomic frame, and low 66 dBA noise profile). A 6-quart backpack vacuum cleans open workstations and stairwells more than twice as fast as an upright while capturing fine allergens.

Heavy-Duty Supply & Restock Transport: Verify that night crews stage paper cases, chemical dilution bottles, and microfiber totes using high-capacity rolling platforms such as the Rubbermaid Commercial Utility Service Cart 3-Shelf (500 lb load capacity across 3 structural foam shelves, 4-in non-marking swivel casters, and rounded trim that protects drywall corners).

ADA-Compliant Restroom & Breakroom Receptacles: Confirm the SOW includes daily sanitization of stainless architectural waste fixtures such as the Simplehuman 55L / 14.5-Gal Commercial Semi-Round Open Can, noting its brushed stainless steel body, lift-off lid for rapid liner swaps, heavy weighted base, and ADA-friendly semi-round wall footprint.

blocks.text: 4-Step Walkthrough to Score and Award Your Janitorial Contract

items.name: Step 1: Conduct a Mandatory Guided Walkthrough With All Bidders
items.text: Walk every contractor through the exact same route, pointing out floor surface transitions (carpet vs. LVT vs. restroom ceramic tile), breakroom appliances, and janitor closet water/storage access so no bidder can claim unforeseen site conditions.

items.name: Step 2: Normalize All Bids to a Standard SOW Bid Sheet
items.text: Require vendors to submit their numbers on your itemized table showing base per-visit rate, 4.33-week monthly total, nightly labor hours, burdened hourly rate ($35–$65/hr), restroom fee ($15–$30/visit), and optional add-ons.

items.name: Step 3: Independent Committee Scoring Using the 100-Point Rubric
items.text: Have Facility Operations, Finance, and HR/Safety independently score each vendor out of 100 points. Average the scores and automatically eliminate any proposal scoring under 75 points or under-allocating nightly man-hours by more than 15%.

items.name: Step 4: Tie the Winning Rubric Score Into a 30-Day SLA Probation Clause
items.text: Attach the winning vendor's promised nightly labor hours, equipment list, and SOW checklist as Exhibit A to the service agreement, backed by weekly joint quality audits during the first 90 days.

faqs.q: What is the minimum passing score on a janitorial SOW evaluation rubric?
faqs.a: Facility procurement teams should set 75 out of 100 points as the minimum qualification threshold, with a mandatory non-negotiable requirement that the bidder score at least 22 out of 30 points in Labor Hour & ISSA Production Realism. Even if a vendor scores well on insurance paperwork and unit price, under-allocating nightly labor hours guarantees dirty restrooms and dusty workstations within the first month.

faqs.q: How do I score a vendor whose production rate exceeds 3,500 sq ft per hour?
faqs.a: The ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hour benchmark applies to standard density commercial offices. If your space is a wide-open tech floor with minimal partitions or polished concrete (0.95x multiplier) and a crew uses 6-quart backpack vacuums and wide dust mops, production rates up to 4,000–4,200 sq ft/hour can earn partial points (20–25 out of 30). However, any bid assuming 4,800+ sq ft/hour in a standard multi-restroom office should receive zero points for labor realism.

faqs.q: Why should equipment specifications carry 15% of the SOW evaluation weight?
faqs.a: Labor productivity and indoor air quality depend directly on tool engineering. A cleaner using a 4-level HEPA commercial backpack vacuum (such as a 6-quart, 11.5 lb unit operating at 66 dBA) and a 500-lb 3-shelf utility cart removes soil 35% faster and traps microscopic particulates that cheap bagless upright vacuums blow back across employee desks.

faqs.q: How should our rubric evaluate quarterly deep floor care proposals?
faqs.a: Verify that quarterly hot-water carpet extraction and VCT machine scrub-and-recoat are priced transparently inside the $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month amortized benchmark (or billed per execution at $55–$95/hour specialty labor) and backed by a fixed calendar schedule specifying the exact months and weekend dates of service.
